newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Islands protest leaders decide to withdraw - HK TV.
newsitem.headline: Islands protest leaders decide to withdraw - HK TV.

text.p: Protest leaders have decided to withdraw from disputed East China Sea islands after some Taiwanese activists made a landing, Hong Kong's Cable TV reported on Monday.
"The command ship has sent an order requiring all boats participating in the protest to retreat 12 nautical miles from the islands," the television reported from the scene.

All protest boats received the order and some, including the command boat of Hong Kong protesters "Pacific 168", were sailing away from the islands claimed by Japan as the Senkakus and Taiwan and China as the Diaoyus, the TV report said.
"It is not immediately known what the protesters will do next after they retreat to the designated areas," a reporter told the TV station.

The protesters landed on the East China Sea archipelago at dawn and raised the national flags of communist China and Taiwan's exiled Republic of China to claim the isles back from Japan but the flags were soon removed by Japanese maritime police, the TV report said.
